title: Analysis kinds and their structure — software-analysis capability
description: Formal shape of the capability's `schemas/artefact-kinds.yaml`: each kind of analysis artefact, and the revalidation record, with the structure its files follow (software-analysis DEC-001 point 1). A structure lists the parts of the kind's body in their order, each with a permanent id, its type, whether it is required, whether it may read `None.`, its hint, its example and the form a script checks in it. It also gives the forms and the hints of the front-matter fields a writer fills, and a collection's file head. The one declaration of each kind's structure. It is the checkable part of the capability's format rule, and binds at that rule's status (DEC-001 point 1; COR-051 point 1). A strict superset of living-docs' `page-kinds.schema.json`: every declaration that schema accepts, this one accepts with the same meaning, since a section that names no type is a heading. Capability data, not adopter data.

kinds.description: The kinds, keyed by the type the capability's places give each artefact kind (DEC-001 point 2; software-analysis DEC-002 point 3), and by a key of its own for the revalidation record, which has no type. Each kind's template is `templates/<kind>.md`, and the glossary's is `templates/glossary.md`.

word.description: A lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

line.description: One line of text, not blank.

sections.description: The elements of the body, in order: for a document kind, its file's body, and for a collection kind, each entry's section. A body may carry other headings and labels besides, and only the declared ones belong to the structure.

ordered.description: Whether the elements come in the order listed. True unless set to false.

shown-as.description: The kind's name as its artefacts show it beside their id, such as `Quality` (software-analysis DEC-002 point 2). A document of the kind is headed `# <id> · <shown-as> · <title>`. An actor, a use case and a journey show none, and are headed `# <id> — <title>`, an actor by its name. A project's own structures relabel no `shown-as`.

retired.description: The ids of elements the kind shipped and retired. An id is permanent once shipped: a retired element is listed here, never renamed, and its id is never given to another element (DEC-001 point 1). A project's addition that names a retired element is an error.

head.description: A collection kind's file head, in order: the elements its file carries once, before the first entry's section. The stamp writes each when it creates the file, and the project may reword it afterwards. A kind with a head is a collection, and its `sections` give each entry's section.

front-matter.description: The front-matter fields a writer fills, each with its hint, its example and, where a script checks one, its form. Where the stamp leaves a field to fill, it writes the field's hint as its placeholder, as it writes a body part's, and the template's front matter, written by hand, shows the same hint. The kind's companion schema checks each field's shape whatever the format rule's status. A form binds at the format rule's status, as every other form does.

section.title: One element of a body: a heading, a label or an opening
section.description: A section that names no type is a heading, as living-docs declares one. An element that names its type names its id too.

id.description: The element's id, unique within its kind, its head included. It is permanent once shipped: an element is retired, never renamed (DEC-001 point 1).

type.description: `heading`: a heading written with one to six `#` at the start of a line. `label`: a bold label, its text then a colon, as `**Goal:**`, that opens a paragraph or a top-level list item. `opening`: the text before the body's first label. `repeated`: a section that repeats, once for each entry of a front-matter list, each headed at its `level` and holding the parts its `sections` give, such as a domain-model view's section for each concept it explains (software-analysis DEC-004 point 2). Every heading of that level is one of its sections, and the stamp writes each heading. Only a declared label marks a part, so a bold run the kind does not declare is content.

sections.description: A repeated section's parts, in order, each held in every one of its sections as a body's element is: an opening, then labels. A part's id is unique within its kind, the elements outside the repeated section included. A repeated section holds no repeated section.

level.description: A heading's level: the number of `#`.

text.description: A heading's text without its `#`, where the kind fixes it, or a label's text without its bold marks and colon. A heading without `text` is one the stamp or the writer words. Text is compared ignoring case, runs of white space and trailing punctuation.

required.description: Whether every artefact of the kind carries the element. True unless set to false. Every element a kind ships is required (DEC-001 point 1).

allows-none.description: Whether the part may read `None.` and nothing else, when it has nothing to say (DEC-001 point 1). False unless set to true.

hint.description: What goes in the part, for whoever fills it. A heading the stamp writes has none.

example.description: An example of what the hint asks for. For a heading the stamp writes, the heading as written.

head-element.title: One element of a collection's file head, with the words the stamp writes for it

id.description: The element's id, unique within its kind, its sections included, and permanent once shipped.

level.description: A heading's level: the number of `#`.

stamp.description: The words the stamp writes for the element when it creates the file: a heading's text without its `#`, or the opening.

form.description: A check on what the element holds, as a body's element takes one. A glossary's opening takes `builds-on-matches-front-matter` (DEC-001 point 2).

field.title: One front-matter field a writer fills

allows-none.description: Whether the field may read `None.` and nothing else, when there is nothing to say yet (DEC-001 point 1; software-analysis DEC-002 point 4). True, it may, and its form is not judged while it does. False, `None.` is refused, at the format rule's status, as every form is. Left out, the field's form alone judges it, so a field that sets neither reads `None.` wherever its form takes it.

hint.description: What goes in the field, for whoever fills it.

example.description: An example of what the hint asks for.

form.description: A check on the content of a part or a front-matter field, from a closed list the capability implements. A list form, such as `numbered-steps`, judges only the part's list items, so a line a writer adds inside the part never breaks it. The `sentence` form is no list form: it judges the whole part as one text.

oneOf.description: One sentence in each text: no sentence ends before the text's last word. The format rule, RS-SAN-001, says what one text is, that a part of this form holds no list, and where a sentence ends.
The part holds at least one list item. Each item opens with a number, and no number repeats. Numbers need not run in sequence, since steps are append-only (DEC-001 point 3).
The part reads `None.`, or holds at least one list item. Each item opens with the number of a step and a letter, such as `2a.`: a step of a use case's main path, or of a journey's steps.

A journey's steps: one numbered item for each entry of the front matter's `steps`, in the same order and numbered from 1, each opening with its number, the use case's id, ` — ` and the use case's title, exactly. A hand-over sits under the step that needs it, and names an earlier step of the journey by its number and id, or a use case outside the journey that the journey relies on (DEC-001 point 4). It opens a line with its bold label, `**Needs from step 2 (UC-005):**` or `**Needs from UC-009 (outside this journey):**`, and text follows it. A line that opens `**Needs from` is a hand-over. Each use case the journey relies on has a hand-over of its own.
A record's outcomes: one top-level item for each entry of the front matter's `outcomes`, in the same order, each opening with `**<id> — <outcome>.**` for its entry, exactly, with text after it.

A record's gaps: the part reads `None.`, or holds one top-level item for each gap. Each item opens with a bold label of one or more ids from `outcomes`, separated by commas and ended by a colon, and holds `**Resolution:**` with text after it. Each artefact whose outcome is `code-regressed` or `gap-found` is named by a gap (DEC-001 point 6).

A glossary's opening, where its front matter's `builds-on` lists what its analysis takes from the analyses it builds on (DEC-001 point 2): one top-level item for each entry, in the same order, opening `**From <analysis> at <version>:**`. Nested in it, one item for each of its terms, `**Term:** [<name>](<link>)`, then for each of its actors, `**Actor:** [<name>](<link>)`, each name exactly its entry's, and nested in an actor's item, one item for each need its entry gives, exactly. Only an item opening `**From ` stands for an entry. Where `builds-on` lists nothing, the form asks nothing.

A repeated section's headings: one section for each entry of the front matter's `explains`, in the same order, each headed by the name of the term the entry names, exactly, white space aside. Where the analysis holds no such term, any heading will do. No two of its headings give one slug, the heading's text in lower case with every character but letters, digits, spaces and hyphens dropped, and each space made a hyphen (COR-050 point 2), so a page anchor on one names one section (software-analysis DEC-004 point 2).

A term's definition, a phrase that could stand in for the term (DEC-001 point 1): its first word is no article, `a`, `an` or `the`, its last character is no full stop, and it holds no whole word of the term's own `name`, in any case.
